items.currentBehavior: Search is a Photon (photon.komoot.io) type-ahead through the same-origin BFF /api/pe-geocode. Every geocoder hit is classified into exactly one of four kinds by classifyFeature() — parcel | address | street | place — and a CITY or COUNTY name falls into the catch-all 'place' bucket. On select, executeSearchLanding case 'place' calls fitExtent(suggestion.extent), which is a bare camera fitBounds to Photon's rectangular bbox with padding 64 / maxZoom 17. NO polygon is drawn, no fill, no outline, no chip. Note the asymmetry: kind 'street' DOES get a visual — highlightStreet() paints a fading cyan rectangle overlay for 4.2s — but 'place' deliberately does not. So today a city/county search recenters the camera on a rectangle and nothing is highlighted. The user cannot see where the jurisdiction actually begins or ends.

items.dataSource: Neon Postgres tables tx_city_boundary (PK geo_id, ~1,225 TxGIO/CPA polygons) and tx_county_boundary (PK county_fips, 254 Census TIGERweb polygons), created by legacy-design-tools migration lib/db/drizzle/0070_tx_city_and_county_boundary.sql. Geometry is GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon in WGS84 stored as jsonb, plus per-row bbox columns (west_lng/south_lat/east_lng/north_lat) with a btree index specifically documented as backing 'viewport pre-filter without decoding jsonb'. CRITICAL: the polygons are in a DATABASE, not a tileset and not a GeoJSON asset. The PE frontend CANNOT access them today — a full-repo grep for txCityBoundary/txCountyBoundary on legacy-design-tools origin/main returns only the ingest CLI, the schema files, and schema/index.ts. There is ZERO read path: no API route, no service, no BFF, no tile build. hauska-map contains no reference to city or county boundaries anywhere.
risks: BLOCKER-CLASS DATA-ACCESS GAP: the '1,222 city + 254 county polygons DONE, LIVE' status is true only about INGEST. The rows exist in Neon and nothing can read them. M1 is not a frontend task — it requires a new server read path in legacy-design-tools (or an engine equivalent) before a single line of PE code can be useful. This is the largest hidden cost in the item and it is invisible from the operator's framing.

PHOTON DOES NOT RELIABLY RETURN COUNTIES. Live probe 2026-08-11: q='Bastrop County' returns 'Bastrop County High Point' (natural=peak) and three parks — the county polygon is NOT in the result set. q='Travis County Texas' returns a courthouse and two cemeteries, no county. Only the BARE name works: q='Bastrop' returns type='county' rank 1 and type='city' rank 2. Since 'Bastrop County' is the natural user phrasing, a naive implementation will highlight nothing for the most common county query. Fix requires stripping a trailing 'County' token before geocoding, or bypassing Photon for jurisdictions entirely and prefix-searching our OWN boundary table (which is the better design — we own 1,225 city + 254 county names and it removes the third-party dependency from the wedge).

VERCEL FUNCTION CAP. apps/property-explorer/api/ currently holds exactly 11 .ts function files and vercel.json documents a Hobby-plan cap of 12; a prior consolidation already collapsed three functions (pe-topography/pe-hydrology/pe-hydrography) into pe-map-layers.ts for exactly this reason. A new /api/pe-boundary function burns the last slot. It MUST fold into pe-map-layers.ts as a layer= branch plus a vercel.json rewrite.

PAYLOAD SIZE. Some Texas city polygons (Houston, Austin, San Antonio ETJ-adjacent shapes) have very high vertex counts, and county polygons carry ~1,200+ ring vertices each (measured: TIGER 48021 = 1,243 vertices). Serving raw jsonb geometry for a statewide set is multi-MB. The OZ layer already solved this with TEXAS_OZ_STATEWIDE_MAX_OFFSET = 0.001 simplification; the boundary route must simplify too, and simplification must not be applied to the polygon used for any in-city legal determination.

SCOPE CREEP INTO ADJUDICATION. The migration comment states the boundary tables exist to enable 'real point-in-polygon in-city determination instead of address-string inference.' If M1 ships a boundary read path, there will be immediate pull to use it for in-city determination too. That is a different, higher-stakes job (it changes what the product ASSERTS about a parcel). Keep M1 strictly cosmetic-highlight and do not let the adjudication ride along on the same PR.

The existing highlightStreet overlay auto-fades after 4.2s. A jurisdiction highlight almost certainly should PERSIST while the user browses that city. That is a UX decision, not a code detail, and the two behaviors should not silently share an implementation.
openQuestions: Should the boundary highlight PERSIST until the next search / an explicit dismiss, or fade like the street highlight (4.2s)? Operator call.

Do we geocode jurisdictions via Photon at all, or serve suggestions from our OWN 1,225-city + 254-county name index? Recommendation: our own — it fixes the 'Bastrop County' failure, removes a third-party dependency from the launch wedge, and the TODO at search-kinds.ts:8 already contemplates first-ranking our own index.

Where does the boundary read route live — legacy-design-tools api-server (where the tables are) or hauska-engine (where PE's other map layers come from via /v1/map-layers/assemble)? This decides which executor owns the lane.
Should ETJ be included? The tables hold incorporated city limits only; ETJ is a separate derivation and the 'etj' layer key already exists in LAYER_REGISTRY marked pending:true.

It is a hand-DECLARED dimension column, and the migration that seeds it says so outright (0068_county_manifest_and_rail_dimension.sql:20-26): 'atom_family_state / has_writer are DECLARED FACTS ... Neither column enforces anything — updating them here does not create an atom or wire a writer; they are the manifest's honest record of what exists elsewhere.' The seeded footprint row (line 110) reads atom_family_state='unpublished', atom_family_ref='building-footprint (contract v1.12.0, unpublished)', has_writer=false, note 'One npm publish away from existing.' Since that seed, the contract published and the engine moved to ^1.19.0 with building-footprint registered in PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES, and the writer landed in three engine commits (32fa049 add county writer, fcf6ad2 stream Texas ML zip, d1a2adb FeatureCollection stream fix). Nobody re-ran countyRailRefreshCli. Because routes/countyLedger.ts:198 gives has_writer=false absolute precedence ('no-writer ... regardless of any stored row'), the grid prints no-writer across all 254 counties even though the writer now exists. SO: the manifest is WRONG about the code and RIGHT about the outcome — a writer exists, but zero footprint atoms have been applied for any county, so no county could serve a footprint today regardless of what the cell says. Do not 'fix' the manifest by flipping has_writer to true; that would replace an honest wrong-reason red with a dishonest green.

ML FOOTPRINTS ARE NOT SURVEY GRADE AND THIS IS A SITE PLAN. Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints are machine-derived from imagery; the writer's own type carries verificationStatus 'machine' | 'human' | 'unsurveyed' and sourceTier 'ml-derived'. A site plan is a document an architect or a city may act on. Drawing an ML-inferred building outline on the same sheet as a surveyed property line, at the same visual weight, invites it to be read as authoritative. Any implementation must visually and textually distinguish the footprint layer as unverified/ML-derived — this is a design constraint on the sheet, not a footnote, and it is exactly the kind of thing the four structural commitments exist to catch.

LICENSE OBLIGATION. ODC-By 1.0 attribution is mandatory and the contract enforces it via a negative guard (ML_FOOTPRINT_SOURCE_CITATION in building-footprint/constants.ts). It must appear on the exported sheet, not merely in the atom payload — an exported PDF/DXF leaves our surface and carries the obligation with it.

THE SERVE PATH IS ALSO MISSING, NOT JUST THE DATA. Even after atoms are applied, hauska-mcp-server's property-atom-chain.ts:24-30 exposes only four slots and its DID regex matches the same four types. Footprint atoms would sit in the database unreachable by PE's export path. This is a third distinct build (apply, serve, render), and the T3 close report already flagged 'serve-surface code not implemented' as a blocker on 2026-08-05.

COST AND SLOT CONTENTION AT SCALE. The ML source is a ~3 GB uncompressed Texas FeatureCollection streamed from a zip and spatially joined per county. The T3 close report records the heavy-scan slot as owned by T1, and repo memory carries an explicit 'serialize heavy DB scans' ruling. A statewide footprint apply is a long heavy job that must be scheduled against that slot, not started opportunistically.

COUNTY CAD FOOTPRINTS DO NOT EXIST AS A SHORTCUT. The recon found 0/11 onboarded counties expose CAD-authoritative footprint polygons on public REST; BCAD's map shows EagleView ortho plus CAMA tabular improvement areas, not a vector layer. There is no higher-quality local source to substitute for ML in the launch counties.

recommendedLaneGrouping: THREE LANES, NOT THREE TASKS — and they are not equal size. LANE 1 (M2, do first, smallest, ships alone): a single executor in hauska-map changes DEFAULT_CENTER + SHARED_DEFAULT_CENTER in lockstep, sets the real initial zoom at map-renderer.js:206, AND — non-optional — adds minzoom to the three parcel layers in parcel-tiles.js and corrects the now-false 'No minzoom gate' comment. Verification must be a live probe of the deployed PE surface measuring cold-open tile bytes, not a merged PR. Ruling needed up front on whether Command Center follows. LANE 2 (M1, second, gated on a server read path): split in two. 2a is a BACKEND lane in legacy-design-tools (or engine) exposing tx_city_boundary / tx_county_boundary over HTTP with simplification, using the OZ statewide route as the working precedent — nothing in PE can start until this lands. 2b is the PE lane: extend SuggestionKind with city/county, strip the trailing 'County' token before geocoding (or better, prefix-search our own boundary names), add a highlightBoundary overlay cloned from highlightStreet, and fold the fetch into pe-map-layers.ts as a layer= branch to respect the 12-function cap. LANE 3 (M3, largest, do NOT dispatch as a UI task): three sequential sub-lanes — (i) run the footprint writer with --apply for at least one county and verify atoms land, contending for the heavy-scan slot; (ii) add building-footprint to the MCP property-atom-chain so the atoms are reachable; (iii) add a footprint slot to the engine SitePlanModel and emit it through DXF/IFC/PDF with ODC-By attribution and explicit ml-derived visual distinction. Sub-lane (iii) is wasted effort until (i) and (ii) exist. SEQUENCING NOTE: M1 and M2 have a real dependency worth exploiting — statewide Texas (M2) is a visually empty landing, and county boundaries (M1's data) are the most natural thing to fill it with. Landing M2 before M1's backend means shipping an empty-looking cold open in the interim.
